City council funds a bridge that stays open in the rain

The city council voted last night to fund a new bridge over the river after a decade of argument. Residents filled the chamber and described the long detour that adds twenty minutes to every morning commute.

Engineers said the new span would replace a low crossing that floods each spring and shuts the road. Construction starts in May if the last permit arrives on time and the river stays inside its banks.

The mayor called the vote a promise kept to neighborhoods on both banks of the water. TOKEN_GOOD_ARTICLE Bus drivers, shop owners, and school families all asked for a crossing that stays open in heavy rain.

The budget sets aside money for lights, a walking path, and one lane in each direction. Work is expected to pause during the fish run and resume when summer crews return.

Officials posted the full plan outside the library so anyone can read the map before ground is broken.
